article.story: JACKSONVILLE, Ala. -- — Caden Creel threw two touchdown passes and added a 22-yard rushing TD in the final 13 minutes to help Jacksonville State overcome a 17-point fourth-quarter deficit and beat Missouri State 25-20 on Saturday. Jacksonville State (8-3, 6-1 Conference USA) has already clinched a berth in the conference championship game against Liberty on Dec. 4. The Gamecocks had 205 of their 417 totals yards in the fourth quarter as they outscore scored the final 21 points to take their first lead when Creel threw a 21-yard touchdown pass to Khristian Lando that made it 25-20 with 5:39 left in the game. Jacksonville State committed nine penalties for 90 yards in the first three quarters but just one for 5 yards in the decisive final 15 minutes. Missouri State (4-7, 3-4) was stopped on fourth-and-goal early in the fourth quarter. Creel threw a deep pass to Jameson Scissum for a 32-yard gain and then hit Deondre Johnson in stride at the 25 on his way to a 59-yard touchdown that capped a four-play, 97-yard drive. The 2-point conversion trimmed the Gamecocks' deficit to 20-11 with 12:41 left in the game. The Bears went three-and-out and Caleb Nix's 16-yard punt return gave JSU possession at midfield. Creel hit Scissums for a 7-yard gain and Lando had a 21-yard catch-and-run to set up Creel's touchdown run made it at two-point game less than 3 minutes later. The Gamecocks defense forced another three-and-out to set up Lando's go-ahead TD reception and then got a fourth-down stop with 1:01 to play that sealed it. Henry Belin IV had 20-of-29 passing for 160 yards, including a 14-yard TD pass to Isaiah Myers for the Bears. Connor Lair had a 79-yard rushing touchdown and finished with 109 yards on 12 carries. Up next Missouri State: Hosts the Liberty Flames next Saturday in the regular-season finale.
